tickets.title: Request to close L train Third Avenue stop
tickets.summary: Joshua Wul, a software engineer, presented a simulation based on 700 million MTA trips. It indicates that closing the L train stop at Third Avenue would save riders about 1,800 hours per day. He asked that the idea go to the transportation committee and that the MTA pilot closing the stop. Action: Refer the request to the transportation committee and consider whether to raise a pilot with the MTA.

tickets.title: Delivery worker e-bike hub on 11th Street
tickets.summary: Over 100 e-bikes used by food delivery workers are stored on the block, obstructing the street and sidewalk. Residents report garbage, a possible fire hazard, closed businesses, and landlords unable to rent units. The 9th Precinct plans an enforcement action and bike confiscation on October 7th. Elected officials and advocacy groups want advance notice, multilingual outreach, and tagging instead of enforcement, and the district manager is still looking for fenced storage sites. Action: District office to keep coordinating with the 9th Precinct, elected officials, and worker groups on notice, outreach, and finding a legal bike storage site, and to hold a follow-up conversation with board members on the history.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark areas in parks
tickets.summary: Callers and speakers report increased drug use and homelessness in Seward Park and Tompkins Square Park. The Seward Park Conservancy and the Lower East Side Ecology Center complained about a bathroom frequented by drug users. Police are monitoring and the district manager says enforcement mostly shifts the problem between parks. A member raised dark spots and unlit areas and asked about mobile crisis teams. Action: District office to follow up with the 7th Precinct and the Parks Department, collect reports of out lights from members via 311 and the office, and look into non-police responses.

tickets.title: Proposed indoor roller skating rink on East River pier
tickets.location_raw: East River Pier across from the Katherine Slip Mall
tickets.summary: Analdi Diaz pitched a 300,000 square foot, three-story multi-use building with an indoor roller skating rink on an East River pier. Admission would be $8 and it is projected to create 250 to 400 direct jobs. Action: Refer the proposal to the land use committee for review.

tickets.title: NYCHA, food, and communication access concerns
tickets.summary: Vincent Jenkins raised struggles with NYCHA housing, lack of food, water, and necessities, and the importance of communication access for deaf and hard of hearing people. He also asked for help with drugs and work opportunities in the community. Action: District office to follow up with Vincent Jenkins on his NYCHA and communication access concerns.

tickets.title: Free public bathroom pilot siting and resolution
tickets.summary: Two free pilot public restrooms are coming to the district, at Delancey and Suffolk and at Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue. DOT leads, installation is planned for mid-October, and a private company will keep them clean for a one-year pilot. The mayor's office asked for suggestions of community partners and locations for tap cards. The committee raised access and emergency-call concerns. Action: Transportation committee to bring a resolution next month setting out concerns and next steps during the pilot, and the office to share partner location suggestions with the mayor's office.

tickets.title: Assign mentor to new board member
tickets.summary: The chair welcomed newest board member Leila Mahia. A mentor will be assigned in the near future. Action: Board leadership to assign a mentor to Leila Mahia.

tickets.title: Second vice chair election
tickets.summary: Daniel Tano and Zachary Thomas were candidates for second vice chairperson and gave speeches before ballots were collected. Daniel Tano won, with 25 votes to Zachary Thomas's 14. Action: Record the result and seat Daniel Tano as second vice chair.

tickets.title: Board trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, procedures
tickets.summary: The chair announced trainings on SLA, Robert's Rules, and office procedures, useful for new members and as a refresher for others. Dates and times are not yet set. Members may email the chair with training topics or questions. Action: Set dates and times for the trainings and report them to members.

tickets.title: Proposed bylaw changes on attendance
tickets.summary: The bylaw task force proposed changes to attendance procedures: an early letter and meeting with the executive committee after too many absences in six months, then possible removal on a second issue. Attendance would be separated from the general removal process, and public members would be bound by conflict of interest policies. A member noted a double-recommendation wording issue. Action: Email the proposed bylaws to all members for the required 28-day notice and hold the vote at the October full board meeting.

tickets.title: District needs statement and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: In October the board will vote on its district needs and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for each agency. Priorities come from committee work throughout the year and agency meetings, and every committee except SLA will discuss them. The goal is to fund programs that need money, such as Summer Youth Employment. Action: Each committee to discuss and finalize its priorities for the October vote.

tickets.title: Comments on city draft housing plan
tickets.summary: The board commented on the city's draft housing plan using positions from the district needs statement. The plan calls for about 7,000 units in five years, 75% of them market rate, and the board's top comment was that affordable housing is the highest need. A member asked about ongoing land use input, and the response was that short turnaround leaves no time for committee review and committees should take positions proactively. Action: Land use committee to take positions proactively on city plans in the future.

tickets.title: Correct SLA resolutions for Cozy Cafe, Soft Hours
tickets.summary: Two August SLA resolutions contain clerical errors. Item number 10 (Soft Hours Tea House) and item number 3 (Cozy Cafe) said they recommend denial of a full on-premises license, but both applicants applied for beer and wine licenses. Action: Correct both resolutions to recommend denial of a beer and wine license unless the applicant agrees to the stipulations.

tickets.title: SLA denial recommendation for Allen Grill
tickets.summary: A motion to flatly deny a full liquor license for item 5 on the August agenda (Allen Grill) passed with 20 yes, 10 no, and 9 abstentions. The operator is formerly of Time Cafe, which residents say has had crowd and stipulation problems, and the location is unlicensed and in a saturated area. Members warned that without community presence at the SLA hearing the license could be granted with no stipulations. Action: Staff to add context on Time Cafe complaints to the resolution, organize members willing to attend the SLA hearing, and watch the SLA calendar.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP community market requirements
tickets.summary: The land use and economic development committees met EDC about the Essex Market RFP, which was due to go out by the end of the month. EDC could not say what had been incorporated from the board's two resolutions on keeping it a community market. The board asked EDC to postpone issuance. Action: Chair of land use, Susan, and the EDC contact to meet later this week to clarify what the RFP includes, then update the board.

tickets.title: Transportation equity analysis priorities with IBO
tickets.summary: Committee leaders and Susan met the Independent Budget Office to assess whether CB3 gets its fair share of transportation resources. About 10 ideas were narrowed to three, including crosstown buses and neighborhood parking locations. Action: Pursue IBO research on crosstown buses and neighborhood parking locations.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge safety and Canal Street update
tickets.summary: The committee sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating the board's concerns at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge, citing the recent crash and death. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project, which has had no update since January. Action: Await responses from DOT and the mayor on the Manhattan Bridge concerns and the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Request congestion pricing impact reporting on FDR
tickets.summary: A member asked whether MTA or DOT will return to discuss congestion pricing, noting the board's resolution about possible increased congestion on the FDR. The member asked whether projections bore out and whether reporting could be requested. Action: Transportation committee to follow up and request reporting from MTA or DOT.

tickets.title: East River Park construction delays and ESCR updates
tickets.summary: Part of the East River Park construction is delayed because of procurement challenges for the new facility that will house the Lower East Side Ecology Center and stewardship programs. The ESCR and BMCR team had little detail on BMCR and will return in October. Community requests for better interim park stewardship support are also pending. Action: Parks committee to have the team return in October with details on the procurement delays and interim stewardship support.

tickets.title: Mobile voting pilot for education council elections
tickets.summary: The Health and Human Services committee presented a resolution supporting a mobile voting pilot for Community and Citywide Education Council elections, where turnout is around 2%. It would be mobile-first, multilingual, accessible, and paired with outreach, and it follows a similar CEC1 resolution. Members raised immigrant family fears and racial and class disparities, and asked for clear messaging that this is school voting only. Action: Vote on the resolution urging NYC public schools to pilot mobile voting and expand outreach, and bring the messaging concerns back to the advocacy provider.
